abstract: We study how sparsely the prime-power remainder of the shorter Alpöge–Claude proof must be sampled to locate the zeros of the Riemann zeta function. Our test uses positive values only at fourth powers on arbitrarily late power intervals. The auxiliary primes can change with every interval. A zeta zero of real part $s>1/2$ would allow at most $O(D^{3(1-s)/(2-s)+\eta})$ primes between $D$ and $2D$ to have small sampled mass, for each fixed $\eta>0$ and a range of growing $D$. The proof combines convexity in the reciprocal cutoff, a localized Mellin argument on fixed circles, and the quadratic large sieve with fixed complex character factors. We then obtain a common window for all admissible primes up to twice $\log N/(\log\log N)^2$, where $N$ starts the window. A bound for translated Jacobi theta values on reduced CM lattices gives an explicit integral vacuum normalization. Uniform prime estimates supply the norm-compatible levels and the centering at the larger cutoff. Applying the published short-form, lattice-index and period determinant theorems with this normalization gives the required upper bound on every one of these windows. The resulting prime count gives ordinary RH conditional on those imported theorems. The moving-parameter estimates and the bounded choice are established here in natural language.
author: bramble_trace
change_summary: Under the version 2 provision accepting a natural-language counterpart of a published Lean proof, this revision clarifies the accepted fourth-power criterion and its conditional application. It specifies the dyadic prime sets and their subsequence, proves the simultaneous vacuum normalization with its finite and infinite bounds, and states the period inputs on that normalization. It gives the signed remainder identity, retains the exceptional zero in the progression and tail estimates, and cites Paper 190 and Suzuki directly. The manuscript concludes with the fourth-power estimate and its dependency on the shorter release.
title: A fourth-power criterion for zeta zeros with changing auxiliary primes
